audit.why: 47.95% over 511 games — a losing but close lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart never gives Ambessa a single stage, including level 6, which the prose calls 'the flip you have been waiting for' and 'your one clearly favoured all-in window'. It also marks level 3 for Irelia where whys[2] says 'genuinely even', and first item for Irelia where whys[5] says 'contested, not owned'.
audit.why: At 47.95% the lane is Irelia's on balance, but not uniformly — Ambessa's 130-second Public Execution suppresses through the one tool Irelia's whole pattern rests on, and that is a real owned stage.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Irelia / Skill / Irelia / Ambessa / Skill / Irelia in both layers — Irelia 3, Skill 3, Ambessa 1, which fits 47.95%. The shape is: she owns the levels either side of your ultimate, you own six itself.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ambessa's level 6 and first-item spikes are both credited to 'the R armor-pen passive', which is not in Riot's text for Public Execution or Drakehound's Step. Irelia's ultimate is not mentioned anywhere on the page, so her level 6 spike is simply missing.
audit.why: Vanguard's Edge is a real spike and a real problem for Ambessa specifically: it Marks the champions it hits, and a Mark refreshes Bladesurge, so her ultimate hands her a free dash; then the blades form a wall that damages and slows anyone walking through, which is the exit Ambessa needs after a dive.
audit.corrected: Penetration claims removed; the 130s / 1250-unit numbers used instead. Vanguard's Edge added to whys[6], spikes[3].text, wants.foe[2] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Bladesurge 'resets on a kill' and stops there, and describes eating Flawless Duet as costing you 'free Q-into-W and passive shred stacking'. Riot's text: Bladesurge refreshes if the target is MARKED or dies; Flawless Duet damages, stuns and MARKS. So the stun is not merely CC — it is the reset enabler. Ionian Fervor also stacks attack speed from spells hitting, with bonus on-hit damage at max stacks; there is no shred in it.
audit.why: The Mark is the whole engine. E onto you means she immediately gets Bladesurge back and dashes onto you again, and R does the same thing later. A player told only 'resets on a kill' will hold their dash for a minion reset that never comes and get run down by a champion whose cooldown just refreshed off the stun that hit them. Second missed interaction: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage while charging, and Ambessa's damage is entirely physical, so W is not a generic block — it is a direct counter to her whole kit, on 20/18/16/14/12s.
audit.corrected: Mark-refreshes-Bladesurge stated in early, wants.foe[1], whys[3] and the interactions line. The physical-damage-reduction wording on Defiant Dance stated in whys[2], whys[5] and mid. 'Passive shred' corrected to attack speed plus on-hit at max stacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice never gives a cooldown for anything.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and Defiant Dance is 20/18/16/14/12s — those are the two windows worth counting, and Defiant Dance is the longer one, which makes it the better thing to bait before an all-in. Bladesurge costs 15 mana on 10/9/8/7/6s and refreshes off Marks, so it is not something you can wait out at all.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in whys[3], mid, wants.you[1] and breakdown.cooldowns, with the all-in keyed to a spent Defiant Dance.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer's content mentions Grievous Wounds, despite Bladesurge healing Irelia on every dash.
audit.why: Bladesurge is a 15-mana ability she casts constantly and it heals her each time. Against a champion who wants extended empowered-auto trades, that sustain is what turns Ambessa's won exchanges into even ones.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal moved into wants.you[2] and named in whys[1] and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vanguard's Edge's wall is never mentioned, and it is the reason a won level 6 does not always become a kill later.
audit.why: Riot: 'Afterwards the blades form a wall that will damage and slow enemies that walk through it.' For a champion who commits with dashes and then needs to leave, a slowing wall dropped behind her is the difference between a trade and a death.
audit.corrected: Added to spikes[3].text, wants.foe[2] and late.

edits.before: Irelia owns the opening — her Q (Bladesurge) dashes through any low minion or onto your body and resets on a kill, so she dances around your single Cunning Sweep while your energy and long early cooldowns leave you flat. Do not step up to throw a cone she just dashes out of; instead manage the wave so her Q-reset paths dead-end, and last-hit at the outer edge where Cunning Sweep doubles. At 3 you finally have E (Lacerate) online: if she Q-dashes onto you, drop the spin so the near-total slow pins her before she can Q to a minion and reset out, and only then commit a Medarda-empowered auto. Respect her E (Flawless Duet) — eating the stun with your dash down means free Q-into-W and passive shred stacking on you.
edits.after: Irelia owns the opening — Bladesurge dashes onto any target, heals her on the way in, and refreshes the moment that target is Marked or dies, so she dances around your single Cunning Sweep while energy and long cooldowns leave you flat. Do not step up to throw a cone she just dashes out of; manage the wave so her reset paths dead-end, and last-hit at the outer edge where Cunning Sweep doubles. At 3 you finally have E (Lacerate): if she Q-dashes onto you, drop the spin so the slow pins her before she can Bladesurge to a minion, and only then commit a Medarda-empowered auto. Respect Flawless Duet — its stun Marks you, and that Mark refreshes Bladesurge instantly, so eating it hands her a free dash straight back onto you.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your worst window and hers to abuse — your cooldowns are longest here and her reset-stun pattern out-trades you, so farm toward 6 and refuse extended fights unless she whiffs a Q. Level 6 is the flip you have been waiting for: Public Execution blinks you behind her and suppresses straight through the Bladesurge mobility she relies on to disengage, and your E-slow plus the R armor-pen passive means she cannot reset away from the all-in. Bait her E stun and her Defiant Dance block first, then R when both are spent — that is the one window where this lane is clearly yours.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your worst window and hers to abuse — your cooldowns are longest while Flawless Duet returns every 16 seconds, so farm toward 6 and refuse extended fights unless she whiffs it. Level 6 is the flip you have been waiting for: Public Execution blinks 1250 units and suppresses straight through the Bladesurge mobility she disengages with, and Lacerate's slow means she cannot reset away from the all-in. Bait Flawless Duet and the Defiant Dance charge first — it cuts physical damage while she holds it, and physical is all you deal — then R once both are spent.

edits.before: This is Irelia's game to reclaim. Once she completes Trinity Force and stacks her passive, her on-hit DPS chunks you through trades, Q-resets keep her glued to you to dodge your E, and Defiant Dance shrugs the burst you need your R for — and your R is on a long cooldown between fights. Your physical-only damage also runs into whatever armor she itemizes. Win or at least heavily pressure the lane around your Level 6 and first-item spike; if it goes even past then, she dances out of your all-ins and takes over as a splitpush threat.
edits.after: This is Irelia's game to reclaim. Once Trinity Force lands and Ionian Fervor stacks, her on-hit DPS chunks you through trades, Vanguard's Edge Marks you for another free Bladesurge and drops a slowing wall across your retreat, and Defiant Dance cuts the physical burst you need your R for — which is 130 seconds between fights. Whatever armour she buys compounds it. Win or heavily pressure the lane around your Level 6 and first-item spike; past that she dances out of your all-ins and takes over as a splitpush threat.

notes: Two derived flags in champ-data/_kits/irelia.json look like tooltip-parse misfires and I did not use either: 'grounding: shuts off enemy dashes' on Flawless Duet (Riot's text is damaged, stunned and Marked — nothing about grounding) and, less clearly, 'zone' on the same ability. The 'terrain' flag on Vanguard's Edge is legitimate — Riot's text does describe the blades forming a wall. Unverified and removed rather than restated: Ambessa's 'R armor-pen passive' (same Ambessa-wide problem as her other matchups) and Ionian Fervor being a shred (it is stacking attack speed, with bonus on-hit at max stacks). One thing I could not verify and therefore left out: whether Public Execution's suppression prevents Irelia from casting Bladesurge at all, or merely stops her moving — the page asserts it 'suppresses straight through Bladesurge' and I kept that wording because suppression is described in the kit as a suppress, but the precise interaction with a dash queued during the blink is exactly what the empty needsResearch block covers.
